A More Human Life｜by Wan @mindfulnesswan

Recently, I've started practicing one thing — when expressing myself, I think within my own framework, no longer predicting and observing others' frameworks to anticipate how I should phrase things to avoid being misunderstood.

For a long time, many of my thought processes have involved attempting to first observe the recipient's framework, then reverse-engineer my expression to land within their understanding.

If I noticed they had misunderstood, that was useful signal: the next attempt would be more precise. But maybe because of age, I have started to tire of this loop. I have also noticed something simpler.

The more I express myself, the rate of being partly understood rises — and the rate of being partly misunderstood rises just as fast. People can only read me through their own experience, and that's fine.
